core_meaning.short_meaning: Articulate, authoritative; early companion and prophetic envoy Salit ibn Amr.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Salit (سَلِيط) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'eloquent, articulate, and commanding in speech' or 'clear-sighted authority'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Salit ibn Amr al-Amiri, one of the earliest converts to Islam who migrated to Abyssinia, fought at Badr, and was selected by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as his diplomatic envoy to the kingdom of Yamama.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from salāṭah (incisive eloquence and commanding clarity of tongue), denoting power of expression and persuasive intellect.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root s-l-ṭ signifies authority, mastery, and articulate clarity. Salit ibn Amr was among the pioneers who embraced Islam in Mecca and suffered persecution. Because of his dignity, eloquence, and diplomatic poise, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ entrusted him with a historic letter to Hawdhah ibn Ali, the ruler of Yamama, calling him to Islam with wisdom and nobility.
